title: Modeling and Simulation Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
description:
About Pratt Miller, an Oshkosh company

Pratt Miller is a product development company in motorsports, defense, and mobility industries providing clients with product engineering and low-volume production solutions. Our range of research & development, engineering, prototype manufacturing, test & validation, and low-rate production capability help our customers bring their high-quality products to market faster.

The Modeling and Simulation Engineering Intern will support engineering activities related to multibody dynamics, vehicle dynamics, durability, and/or multi-physics simulation. The intern will work with experienced engineers to build, run, post-process, and evaluate simulation models used for product development.

This position is intended to provide hands-on experience with engineering simulation workflows, test and simulation data analysis, model correlation, and technical problem solving. Assignments will be scoped to the intern's experience level and completed with guidance from engineering team members.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND SKILLS:

Typical responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Assist with multibody dynamics modeling, vehicle performance analysis, and co-simulation activities.

  • Build, modify, run, and post-process simulation models of vehicles and mechanical systems under the guidance of experienced engineers.

  • Support comparison and correlation of simulation results with physical test data.

  • Assist with development of scripts and tools for simulation setup, data processing, visualization, and reporting.

  • Work with engineering teams such as design, test, controls, and manufacturing to support project activities.

  • Document model assumptions, analysis methods, results, and conclusions.

  • Participate in technical discussions, design reviews, and team meetings.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, team-oriented environment.

  • Willingness to learn new engineering tools, methods, and technical concepts.

  • Excellent time management and organizational skills.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to ask questions, receive feedback, and apply lessons learnt.

  • Dependable attendance and accountability for assigned tasks.

  • Commitment to quality, safety, and continuous improvement.

EDUCATION/CERTIFICATION/YEARS OF EXPERIENCE:

  • Completion of foundational coursework in dynamics, mechanics, controls, numerical methods, or related subjects is preferred.

  • Previous internship, Formula SAE/Baja SAE, research, laboratory, design-team, or engineering project experience is beneficial but not required.

DESIRED SPECIALIZED SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE:

The following skills are desirable but are not required. Candidates are not expected to have experience in all areas listed.

  • The following skills are desirable but are not required. Candidates are not expected to have experience in all areas listed.

  • Exposure to multibody dynamics or simulation tools such as Adams, Dymola, Simscape.

  • Familiarity with MATLAB/Simulink, Python, C++, or similar programming languages.

  • Basic understanding of mechanical systems, vehicle dynamics, and controls.

  • Familiarity with engineering data analysis, plotting, and interpretation.

  • Exposure to signal processing, test data analysis, or data acquisition systems.

  • Strong analytical thinking, curiosity, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work independently on well-defined tasks while seeking guidance when needed.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Ability to work safely in office, laboratory, shop, or test environments as required by assigned projects.

  • Ability to lift and move light engineering equipment or components in accordance with company safety requirements.

EXPECTED HOURS OF WORK:

  • Standard work hours will follow department and company internship guidelines.

  • Some schedule flexibility may be required to support testing, project milestones, or team activities.

Pay Range:

$18.00 - $37.00

The above pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target pay for the position across all U.S. locations. Within this range, individual pay is determined by various factors, including the scope and responsibilities of the role, the candidate's experience, education and skills, as well as the equity of pay among team members in similar positions. title: Senior Software Engineer-AI Enabled Development
description:
Senior Software Engineer-AI Enabled Development

Valor is the leader in mineral management, oil and gas accounting and oil and gas consulting. The company was built by multi-generational mineral owners and experienced mineral managers to bring peace of mind to mineral and royalty owners. Valor utilizes its proprietary best-in-class mineral management software, mineral.tech®, to efficiently and effectively manage minerals and royalties for our clients. Valor is headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas. We provide solutions for owners of oil and gas assets which include comprehensive land and mineral rights management solutions, oil and gas accounting, digital filing, division order processing, and other oil and gas related back-office solutions that can be tailored to your specific needs.

Location: Fort Worth, Texas

About the Company

Valor is a fast-growing innovation company headquartered in Fort Worth, TX. We are a leader in oil and gas outsourcing, accounting, business strategy, and consulting for the energy industry and have developed a best-in-class mineral management software, mineral.tech, to efficiently and effectively manage minerals and royalties for our clients.

The Opportunity

We're seeking a Senior Software Engineer with strong full-stack expertise and hands-on experience utilizing AI agents in the development of modern SaaS products. You'll lead the technical direction for multiple applications — with primary focus on our core SaaS platform. This is a builder + leader role: you'll write critical code, architect scalable systems, utilize AI agents for feature development, and deliver fast and reliably.

You will define the plan for complex business problems and manage those projects to completion. You should be opinionated about best practices but flexible enough to work with senior leadership to meet business goals. You will also be expected to use AI as a primary tool to speed up development and create intelligent features.

To be considered for the position, all candidates must complete the following two assessments:

  • Lead end-to-end development of new product modules, features, and customer-facing apps while ensuring high performance, security, and observability.
  • Directly manage and mentor a team of Software Engineers as well as Agents: conduct code reviews, provide technical guidance, support career growth, run performance processes, and participate in hiring, if necessary.
  • Architect, build, and scale our primary SaaS platform and supporting applications using Django/Python (backend), React (frontend), Celery and Redis (task queues and caching), PostgreSQL, and PostGIS for geospatial capabilities.
  • Design and implement AI agent integrations (using frameworks like Google ADK, LiteLLM, Gemini) to power intelligent features.
  • Own system design decisions, database schemas (including spatial data modeling with PostGIS), API architecture, and deployment pipelines.
  • Collaborate closely with product, design, data, and customer success teams to translate requirements into reliable, AI‑enhanced software.
  • Drive best practices in testing, CI/CD, monitoring, scalability, and cost optimization in cloud environments (AWS preferred).
  • Stay current with advancements in AI agents and full‑stack technologies to continuously improve our platform.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong full‑stack development background.
  • Proven experience utilizing AI agentic development, including scalable human review workflows and systems. May be asked to demonstrate production examples where AI has accelerated or improved your outcomes.
  • Experience implementing AI in applications (e.g., LLM‑powered agents, multi‑agent systems, tool usage, memory/RAG patterns).
  • Track record of successfully leading and managing software engineering teams (formal management experience with onshore/nearshore/offshore).
  • Solid understanding of SaaS architecture: authentication (e.g., Auth0, JWT), multi‑tenancy, scalability, REST API design, and cloud deployment.
  • Experience with CI/CD tools (GitHub Actions), observability platforms (Elasticsearch/Kibana, Sentry), and infrastructure automation.
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills; must be based in (or willing to relocate to) the Fort Worth area.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Working knowledge of the oil and gas industry.
  • Experience shipping AI‑enhanced SaaS products at scale (handling thousands of users, agent‑driven automation).
  • Familiarity with geospatial applications using PostGIS.
  • Experience migrating legacy frontend frameworks (e.g., AngularJS) to modern React architectures.
  • Familiarity with data warehouse integrations (Snowflake) and document processing pipelines.
  • Prior work in startup/scale‑up environments with rapid iteration.
  • Open‑source contributions or personal projects showcasing AI agents in web apps.

title: Graduate Assistant: Esports Coach
description:
North Park University, a member of the College Conference of Illinois and Wisconsin, would like to announce that applications are now being accepted for the position of Esports Graduate Assistant Coach. The assistantship will begin in August 2026 and includes tuition remission, a partial meal plan, and a $3,000 stipend per semester.

About North Park
Founded in 1891, North Park University is a Christian university affiliated with the Evangelical Covenant Church of over 3,200 students from around the country and the world. Located for over 125 years on the land of the Miami and Potawatomi tribes in what is today Chicago’s northside, NPU has recently been designated a Hispanic Serving Institution and is committed to serving diverse populations. Elevating North Park University’s core distinctives of Christian, city-centered, and intercultural, NPU values diversity among its faculty and is committed to building a racially and culturally diverse intellectual community, and strongly encourages the nomination and candidacies of persons who are Black, Indigenous, and People of Color regardless of gender.

North Park University is located in the Albany Park neighborhood of Chicago, one of the most ethnically diverse zip codes in the United States. It is nine miles from downtown Chicago. The North Park campus has often been referred to as an oasis in the heart of the city – a place where students from urban, rural, and suburban backgrounds alike can call home. And all of this within the major metropolitan backdrop of Chicago: one of the world’s largest and most diversified economies, renowned for its museums and music, and voted best large city in the U.S. for four years in a row by Condé Nast Traveler.

Mission

The mission of North Park University is to prepare students for lives of significance and service through education in the liberal arts, professional studies, and theology.

Vision

Building on our core institutional identity—Christian, city-centered, intercultural—our vision is to create a university of uncommon character and enduring excellence, where faith, learning, and service meet.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assists the Director of Esports with the daily operations of the Esports program at North Park University.
  • Analyze performance and instruct athletes in gaming techniques and strategies in preparation for and during competition.
  • Assist with all phases of competitive recruiting.
  • Execute practice and tournament planning/evaluation, including video exchange and breakdown.
  • Ensure a commitment to the academic success of Esports student-athletes, including monitoring academic performance, attendance, and social behavior.
  • Build and sustain positive relationships with student-athletes, parents, alumni, faculty, staff, and the campus community.
  • Have a working knowledge of and a commitment to intercollegiate Esports rules and regulations.
  • Complete other duties as assigned by the Director of Esports, Assistant Vice President for Athletics and Sport Management, and Associate and

Requirements

  • A bachelor’s degree is required.
  • Applicant must obtain acceptance in a North Park University graduate program.
  • Applicant must be able to work an untraditional work schedule (i.e. frequent nights and weekends).
  • Coaching or playing experience and extensive knowledge of the Esports are required.
  • Able to travel with team, by vehicle or plane.
  • A valid driver’s license is required.; Use of personal vehicle to travel to/from practice and or competition.
  • Possess a clear understanding and personal commitment to North Park’s mission of Christian higher education.

title: Senior Energy Consultant/Building Physicist
description:
Civic is a team of system thinkers in the built environment, creating positive impact for people, places and the planet.

We want our work to have a positive impact on the environment — helping people to live healthier, happier lives while respecting natural limits. We build without destroying, explore without exploiting, and seek to reuse rather than just consume. Above all, we listen, learn, and aim to create a lasting legacy.

Thriving together, today we have a team of over 200 members working across the UK, all united by our creative belief, bringing art and science together to solve problems. Our award-winning practice has studios in Manchester, London, Leeds, Glasgow, Edinburgh and Dublin

Requirements

As a Senior Energy Consultant / Building Physicist, you will take responsibility for defined workstreams and smaller projects, while supporting senior colleagues on larger or more complex commissions. You will be expected to understand the wider design context, not simply produce modelling outputs, and to translate technical findings into clear recommendations that influence the architectural and engineering design.

The role will suit someone who enjoys combining analytical work with consultancy, is comfortable presenting findings to clients and design teams, and wants to develop further expertise in operational energy, advanced HVAC modelling and performance-led design.

Day-to-day task and expectations

  • Lead and deliver dynamic thermal modelling using IES VE across concept, planning, detailed design and post-completion stages.
  • Undertake whole-building energy, comfort, overheating, natural ventilation and passive-design assessments for residential and commercial developments.
  • Use relevant IES VE applications such as ApacheSim, MacroFlo, SunCast and VistaPro to test design options and interpret performance.
  • Develop robust models from architectural, structural and MEP information, clearly recording assumptions, limitations and inputs.
  • Review fabric, glazing, shading, ventilation, heating, cooling, lighting and controls strategies and advise on their effect on energy use and occupant comfort.
  • Translate modelling results into practical, proportionate recommendations for architects, engineers, developers and contractors.
  • Undertake and coordinate Part L compliance assessments for residential and non-domestic buildings, including SAP, SBEM, BRUKL and associated reporting as appropriate to the project.
  • Support the preparation and review of Energy Performance Certificates and related compliance evidence, working within relevant accreditation requirements.
  • Deliver overheating assessments in accordance with appropriate guidance, including CIBSE TM52 and TM59, and explain the design implications to project teams.
  • Undertake or coordinate daylight and sunlight assessments where required, using the results to support design development and planning submissions.
  • Prepare high-quality planning-stage Energy Statements, Sustainability Statements, Overheating Assessments, Daylight Reports and other technical notes.
  • Respond to planning conditions, Building Control comments and technical queries, maintaining a clear audit trail of assumptions and design changes.
  • Keep informed of changes to UK building regulations, planning policy, industry guidance and energy-assessment methodologies.
  • Develop energy and sustainability strategies that balance carbon performance, occupant comfort, planning policy, buildability, programme and cost.
  • Work collaboratively with mechanical, electrical, public health, structural and civil engineers, architects and specialist consultants.
  • Attend client, design team and coordination meetings, presenting technical information clearly and confidently.
  • Manage agreed tasks, deliverables, budgets and programmes, identifying risks or information gaps at an early stage.
  • Review project information and modelling inputs for completeness and coordinate the information required from other disciplines.
  • Support construction-stage queries, review contractor proposals where relevant and assist with post-completion performance evaluation.
  • Build trusted relationships with clients and project teams by providing responsive, practical and evidence-based advice.
  • Contribute to fee proposals, scopes of service, bids and work-winning material, including estimating the effort required for modelling and reporting tasks.
  • Apply internal quality assurance procedures and take ownership of the technical accuracy, clarity and presentation of deliverables.
  • Mentor graduate and junior consultants, including reviewing models, calculations and reports and providing constructive feedback.
  • Contribute to internal knowledge sharing, templates, guidance and the continuous improvement of modelling and reporting workflows.
  • Support innovation in analysis tools, automation and data-led design methods that improve efficiency and technical quality.

Behaviour and Professional Commitment

  • Proactive and solutions-focused, with the judgement to identify what matters most to a project.
  • Able to turn complex modelling results into clear design actions rather than presenting data without interpretation.
  • Commercially aware and mindful of scope, programme, budget and the level of detail appropriate to each project stage.
  • Collaborative and approachable, with the confidence to challenge assumptions constructively when evidence supports it.
  • Committed to high technical standards, continuous learning and the professional development of colleagues.
  • Practical in outlook, recommending solutions that are deliverable, proportionate and aligned with the client brief.

Experience/Qualifications Required

  • Typically 3-5 years of relevant professional experience in building physics, energy and sustainability consultancy, environmental design or building services engineering.
  • Experience delivering building performance analysis for residential and/or commercial buildings across more than one project stage.
  • Experience of SAP and/or SBEM assessments, with sufficient understanding to coordinate both residential and commercial project requirements.
  • Experience undertaking overheating and comfort assessments using CIBSE TM52 and/or TM59.
  • A relevant degree or equivalent experience in building services engineering, environmental engineering, architecture, physics, sustainability or a related discipline.
  • Experience using ApacheHVAC to model HVAC systems, controls and operational performance in greater detail.
  • Knowledge of NABERS UK and Design for Performance, including target-setting, simulation, independent design review and the performance gap.
  • Experience applying CIBSE TM54 for operational energy prediction and understanding the use of TM46 benchmarks or other performance data.
  • Experience with both residential and commercial compliance, including relevant assessor accreditation such as OCDEA and/or NDEA.
  • Experience of daylight modelling, natural ventilation analysis, passive design studies or climate-based design assessment.
  • Familiarity with BREEAM energy credits, embodied and whole-life carbon considerations, low and zero carbon technology studies, or planning policy carbon targets.

Benefits

💰A fair and competitive salary, taking into consideration market rates and your experience level

🫶Flexibility. Our core hours are between 10:30am-4:30pm, with an early Friday finish!

⚖️Hybrid working. Most of our full-time employees come into the studio 3 days a week

🌴Generous holidays! 26 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays (pro-rata for part time employees). An extra day when you reach 3 years’ service, and another at 5 years!

🌞Holiday options. Buy or sell a week of holiday each year, or create a sabbatical pot by banking a week’s holiday for 3 years to take a month off on year 4!

👪 Enhanced Family Leave. Enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental and neonatal care leave pay, plus 2 days paid dependency leave and 1 weeks paid carers leave

🌱Wellbeing support. Mental health first aider support, mindfulness sessions and access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)

🩹Health benefits. Life Assurance, Health Care Cash Plan, Gym discounts and free Eye tests

🤒Sick Pay. 4 weeks enhanced sick leave, plus 2 mental wellness days

⭐DEI network. An established Equity, Diversity and Inclusion network with regular team activities, plus 2 days of paid volunteering leave each year to support causes close to your heart

💡 Professional Development. Paid professional memberships, 2 days paid study leave (+ extra for exams), Chartership Preparation Courses, Chartership completion bonus, in-house ‘Civic Academy’ training, Management Development Programmes and a Mentorship programme for all employees

💷Financial benefits. Access to our HMRC friendly Workplace Nursery scheme, plus enrolment to our workplace pension scheme

🚆Sustainable travel. Season Ticket Loans & National Rail Cards, plus two salary sacrifice cycle to work schemes and cycling facilities at all our studios (showers, bike racks etc).

title: 26-27 School Year: Before/After-care Group Leader
description:
About DeKalb Brilliance Academy: Designed with input from nearly 1,000 South DeKalb community members, DeKalb Brilliance Academy is a tuition-free, public K–8 charter school committed to building a fundamentally different kind of education. We currently serve grades K–6 and will add one grade per year (learn more about our founding journey here).

Our vision is that each child will know and leverage their unique brilliance to critically analyze the world around them and to design a better and more equitable future. We pursue this vision through our Career-connected Project-based Learning, where students learn not only from their teachers and peers, but also directly from scientists, lawyers, engineers, and designers. Our model is ambitious by design - and built to challenge the status quo in service of our students and community.

DeKalb Brilliance Academy: where the strength of our community nurtures the brilliance of our children.

About the before/after-care program (The Hive): The Hive is the before-care and after-school program at DeKalb Brilliance Academy. We serve scholars from the moment the building opens until the last family leaves, and our work is built on the belief that the hours outside the school day matter as much as the ones inside it. Our programming is guided by five pillars — Love, Learning, Leadership, Creativity, and Community — and by four commitments we make to each other: we care, we correct, we learn, we grow.

About the role: The Group Leader is a front-line program leader responsible for designing and facilitating engaging, structured, and age-appropriate activities during the after-school day. This role shapes the scholar experience, supports positive behavior, and brings the pillars to life through enrichment, movement, creativity, and group engagement. Group Leaders work directly with scholars and collaborate closely with site leadership to ensure activities are safe, engaging, inclusive, and aligned with program goals.

  • Position Group Leader: assigned to one grade band
  • Reports to Senior Program Director
  • Employment type: Part-time, hourly, non-exempt
  • Hours Approximately; 25 hours per week
  • Calendar: school days only
  • Benefits: This position does not include benefits or paid sick time

Responsibilities

Activity planning and delivery

• Design, plan, and facilitate engaging, age-appropriate activities aligned with the pillars

• Prepare daily activity plans that balance structure, creativity, movement, and scholar choice

• Set up, manage, and reset your activity space before and after programming

• Ensure activities are safe, inclusive, and accessible to every scholar in your group

Supervision and scholar engagement

• Take paper attendance within the first five minutes of program

• Move scholars at Level 0, with an adult positioned mid-to-back of the line

• Build positive, respectful relationships with scholars while holding professional boundaries

Behavior support

• Reinforce clear expectations and routines during every activity

• Address minor concerns through redirection, coaching, and de-escalation

• Use restorative language — we reset, we do not use time-out

• Move a scholar's seat early, before a moment escalates

• Log every behavior incident the same day it happens

Documentation and communication

• Complete attendance, incident reports, and activity documentation accurately and on time

• Communicate with families only as directed by program leadership

• Keep your walkie on you and turned all the way up for your entire shift

• Tell leadership before your shift, not after, if anything will affect your arrival

Materials, space, and closeout

• Complete the nightly clean sweep: tables wiped, floor swept, all program materials removed, chairs in

• Power P-boards fully off — not screen-off — and confirm the indicator light is out

• Leave every shared space reset and ready for the school day the next morning

• Be checked out by a member of the leadership team before you leave

Health, safety, and supervision

• Maintain active supervision at all times — proximity, scanning, and positioning

• Your back is never to scholars. Two adults in a space stand opposite each other, never side by side

• Conduct headcounts at every transition, at every activity, and at dismissal

• Know the allergies, medical needs, and safety plans of every scholar in your care

• Follow all health, safety, and supervision policies in the Staff Handbook

• Support emergency procedures and drills, and know your assignment on the Building Response Team

Mandated reporting and scholar protection

• Serve and assume all responsibilities as a program-based mandated reporter

• Report any suspected child abuse, neglect, or safety concern in accordance with Georgia law

• Escalate safety, injury, abuse, or family matters to leadership immediately, even if the picture is incomplete

• Maintain professionalism, confidentiality, and discretion on all sensitive matters

This role is responsible for other duties as assigned.

To see fuller job description, please click here.

Requirements

Experiences

  • Minimum two years previous experience is strongly preferred
  • All candidates must be able to pass a DECAL background check
  • All candidates are required to be able to meet the physical demands of the role (including standing and walking for extended periods of time and lifting heavy objects up to 40lbs)

Who Thrives at DeKalb Brilliance

DeKalb Brilliance Academy is a great fit for individuals who are:

  • Purpose-driven: have deep reverence for the brilliance of our children and unwavering commitment to empowering our children to have impactful legacies in our communities
  • Community-minded: has ability work collaboratively with peers and manage up to improve the work of everyone around them
  • Emotionally intelligent: knows how to care for themselves, collaborate with others, use tools to regulate their emotions under stress, and approach difficult situations with others with empathy and compassion
  • Equity-minded: understand how specific behaviors, laws, and institutions limit the rights and freedoms of people and work with our community to take collective action to make our world fairer for everyone.
  • Strong project and time managers: has ability to adapt and persevere to deliver consistent and timely results to reach our goals
  • Have a founder’s mindset: is a creative problem solver, enjoys building from the ground up

Benefits

    • Hourly rate is commensurate with experience
    • Compensation is based on school days only

Statement of Non-Discrimination:

DeKalb Brilliance Academy is committed to a policy of equal treatment for all individuals applying for employment. DeKalb Brilliance Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, handicap, age, religion, sexual orientation, or national or ethnic origin.

title: Operations Assistant
description:
Think Business Loans is a fast-growing finance broker that specialises in providing alternative finance solutions for small and medium-sized businesses in the UK. Think is the finance division of Bionic, the UK's leading business comparison service, and has become the largest finance broker of its kind in the country.

Think's unique approach combines cutting-edge technology with human expertise to deliver an exceptional service to our clients. This allows us to provide tailored finance solutions that meet the unique needs of each business we work with. Our approach streamlines the application and approval process for maximum efficiency, whilst always maintaining a personal and professional approach to finance.

Think Business Loans is part of the Bionic Group. We focus on using state-of-the-art matching and tendering platforms, and our expert lending managers help SME’s save time, money, and hassle on their business loans.

The role

We’re looking for a highly organised and proactive Operations Assistant to support the smooth day-to-day running of one of our sales pods within Think Business Loans.

You’ll play an essential role in managing business finance applications from submission through to completion. Working closely with sales agents, lenders and customers, you’ll ensure applications are packaged accurately, progress efficiently through underwriting and receive the attention needed to deliver the best possible customer outcome.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys bringing structure to a fast-paced environment, building strong working relationships and solving problems. If you’re detail-focused, commercially aware and motivated by delivering excellent service, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

Application Management & Quality Assurance

  • Conduct thorough quality assurance checks on applications, ensuring each one is packaged accurately and to a high standard before submission.
  • Monitor live applications and help them progress efficiently through the underwriting process.
  • Work with sales agents and, where necessary, customers to obtain documentation or additional information requested by lenders.
  • Keep application records and ThinkApp statuses accurate and up to date, clearly reflecting the current position of each case.

Sales Support

  • Work closely with sales agents, supporting them with product placement and up-to-date lender knowledge.
  • Provide timely updates on applications that are progressing through underwriting.
  • Ensure sales agents remain informed and have the operational support they need throughout the application journey.

Lender Relationships

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with lenders, acting as the primary lender liaison for your pod.
  • Monitor lender service-level agreements and help ensure applications continue to progress within the required timescales.
  • Negotiate offers directly with lenders to help secure favourable outcomes for customers.

Operational Excellence

  • Manage the tender's mailbox for your pod, ensuring queries and tasks are dealt with promptly.
  • Maintain clear and accurate information throughout the application lifecycle.
  • Identify process gaps and suggest improvements that could increase efficiency across the pod.
  • Help create a well-organised, responsive environment in which sales agents, lenders and customers are effectively supported.

About you

We’re looking for someone who combines excellent organisation with strong attention to detail and a genuine desire to help others succeed. You’ll be comfortable managing several live priorities, communicating with different stakeholders and taking ownership of tasks through to completion.

You’ll likely have:

  • Excellent attention to detail and a consistently accurate approach to your work.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple applications and priorities.
  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication skills.
  • A proactive approach to problem-solving and progressing outstanding actions.
  • Confidence building positive working relationships with colleagues, lenders and customers.
  • The ability to work effectively in a fast-moving, target-driven environment.
  • A collaborative mindset and a willingness to support the wider sales pod.
  • The confidence to identify inefficiencies and recommend practical improvements.

Required skills & experience

  • Experience in an administrative, operational, sales-support or customer-service environment.
  • Strong IT literacy and confidence using business systems and shared mailboxes.
  • The ability to maintain accurate records and manage detailed information.
  • Experience communicating professionally with internal and external stakeholders.
  • The ability to prioritise work and respond promptly to changing business needs.

Desirable skills & experience

  • Experience supporting finance, lending, brokerage or application-based processes.
  • Previous experience working with lenders or other third-party providers.
  • Experience conducting quality checks or reviewing applications and supporting documentation.
  • Knowledge of underwriting processes or service-level agreements.
  • Experience using a CRM, application-management platform or similar operational system.

The interview process

  • Initial conversation via Teams with one of our Talent Acquisition Specialists
  • Final stage in person interview with the Hiring Manager

About Bionic Group

Bionic has over 600 people working across three office locations and four businesses; Bionic - London, Bionic Outbound – Luton, Think Business Loans – Chelmsford, Utility Bidder – Corby and Smart – Field based agents.

We have a high energy work environment wherever the location; you can feel the passion the moment you walk through our door! Our work environments are packed with amazing people and energy, hubs of collaboration, creativity and fun! We’re one team, we get stuck in, we roll our sleeves up and we care about helping each other out wherever we can. We set the highest standards and show up every day to be the best version of ourselves.

Working at Bionic means provides you many opportunities to advance your career, with incredible progression, recognition, and reward.

Benefits

We know that our employees are what sets us aside from our competitors, our benefits are just part of the way we say thanks.

Enhance your health & wellbeing 🌱

  • Private healthcare cover
  • Employee Assistance Programme, including a virtual GP service, priority physio & talking therapies
  • Eyecare scheme

Taking time away from work 🏖️

  • 25 days annual leave plus the 8 UK bank holidays, increasing with tenure
  • 1 paid family/religious day of leave per year - following successful probation period
  • 1 paid charity volunteering day per year
  • Option to buy/sell up to an additional 3 days leave per year

Family matters: for the special moments 🏠

  • Enhanced maternity, paternity or shared parental leave
  • 2 days off for your wedding upon joining, and up to 5 days after 2 years' service
  • Flexible working options & a hybrid work approach

Financial wellbeing 💸

  • Auto-enrolled salary sacrifice pension scheme
  • Life assurance
  • Season ticket Loans, salary advances & loans to buy/rent a home – based on tenure

The Healthcare Designer bridges clinical functionality and architectural design. Operating as part of an independent, open-line dealership and consultancy network (working across top lines like Kimball, HNI, Bernhardt, OFS/Carolina, Nucraft, and medical vendors), this role translates medical equipment needs, room matrices, and clinical workflows into accurate, fully coordinated BIM models and interior space plans. This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Pessoa Coordenadora de Segurança Ofensiva (Red Team) based in Brazil.

This is a remote, full-time leadership opportunity focused on strengthening offensive cybersecurity capabilities across a complex technology environment.
You will lead the planning and coordination of realistic cyberattack simulations, penetration tests, and advanced threat emulation activities.
The role combines Red Team leadership with responsibility for vulnerability management and application security initiatives.
You will continuously assess the organization’s attack surface, prioritize risks, and validate the effectiveness of preventive, detective, and responsive security controls.
Working across offensive, defensive, engineering, architecture, and governance teams, you will help embed security into technology and software development practices.
You will also develop technical talent, establish performance indicators, and drive continuous improvements across security programs.
The position offers the opportunity to shape cybersecurity strategy while helping protect sensitive assets and support regulatory and organizational requirements.

Accountabilities:

  • Offensive Security Leadership: Plan, coordinate, and supervise offensive security campaigns, including penetration testing, Red Team operations, and controlled simulations of advanced persistent threats, ensuring all activities are ethical, secure, controlled, and aligned with corporate policies.
  • Security Methodologies and Operations: Develop, implement, and continuously improve methodologies, processes, and tools for offensive security operations while keeping practices aligned with emerging threats, tactics, techniques, and industry standards.
  • Vulnerability Management: Coordinate infrastructure vulnerability management programs, ensuring adequate coverage of critical technology assets and establishing strategies for vulnerability identification, classification, prioritization, remediation, and ongoing tracking.
  • Application Security: Coordinate application and secure-code vulnerability management throughout the software development lifecycle, promoting Application Security, DevSecOps, Secure by Design, and Secure Coding practices across development teams.
  • Security Validation: Continuously assess technical vulnerabilities, process weaknesses, and security control gaps while validating the effectiveness of preventive, detective, and responsive controls through offensive and Purple Team activities.
  • Attack Surface Monitoring: Monitor the organization’s cyber exposure across on-premises and cloud environments, networks, operating systems, databases, applications, and other technology assets, ensuring risks are identified and addressed according to business impact.
  • Risk Metrics and Governance: Define and monitor KPIs, maturity metrics, remediation SLAs, and other performance indicators for Red Team, Vulnerability Management, and AppSec programs, providing clear reporting to relevant stakeholders.
  • Team Development: Coordinate, develop, and coach the Offensive Security team, encouraging technical growth, knowledge sharing, collaboration, and integration with other cybersecurity and technology functions.
  • Regulatory and Audit Support: Support regulatory processes, internal and external audits, compliance assessments, and other governance activities by providing relevant technical information and evidence related to cybersecurity controls and practices.
  • Security Culture: Promote cybersecurity awareness across the organization and encourage the adoption of stronger security practices through collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

    • Requirements

    • Vulnerability and AppSec Programs: Experience coordinating Vulnerability Management and/or Application Security programs, including vulnerability prioritization, remediation tracking, and integration of security practices into software development.
    • Offensive Security Knowledge: Strong knowledge of penetration testing, defense evasion, controlled attack simulations, Purple Team activities, MITRE ATT&CK, and Attack Surface Management.
    • Application Security: Familiarity with application security architecture, SSDLC, DevSecOps, OWASP Top 10, API security, SAST, DAST, SCA, IAST, and CI/CD pipeline security.
    • Infrastructure and Cloud Security: Knowledge of Windows and Linux operating systems, Active Directory and Microsoft environments, corporate networks and communication protocols, cloud security across Azure, AWS and/or GCP, containers, and Kubernetes.
    • Certifications: OSCP, OSEP, and OSWE certifications are desirable and demonstrate relevant offensive security expertise.
    • Strategic and Behavioral Skills: Strong leadership and people-development capabilities, strategic cybersecurity risk awareness, influencing and negotiation skills, analytical and investigative thinking, risk-based decision-making, results orientation, collaboration, adaptability, and continuous learning.

title: QA Engineer – AI Automation
description:
Job Title: QA Engineer – AI Automation

About Assembly Industries

Assembly Industries is The Workforce Modernization Company. For fifty years, software — the single greatest lever for business efficiency and productivity — has been gated behind two doors: buy it from a vendor, or hire an engineering team to build it. Coding agents have fundamentally changed that. Our mission is to make every employee a builder: we convert often non-technical subject-matter experts into prolific builders of software through training, a platform to execute on, and a partner standing beside them every day after launch.

Assembly Platform is our end-to-end application lifecycle platform — from problem discovery and requirements through architecture, production deployment with IT, adoption, and ongoing maintenance. The prototype is just the tip of the iceberg; Assembly Platform and our team handle everything below the waterline. Our vision is to help existing businesses build their own software operating system from the inside out.

Role Overview

As a QA Engineer, you will be responsible for ensuring the reliability, performance, and scalability of our AI-powered automation products. You will own the end-to-end quality assurance process—designing and executing test strategies, building automated test frameworks, and pioneering the use of AI-driven QA approaches across multiple products.

This role is perfect for someone with a strong software engineering background who is passionate about quality, eager to explore cutting-edge QA technologies, and thrives in the fast-paced environment of a startup.

What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)

Test Strategy & Planning

  • Define and execute comprehensive QA strategies for AI automation products.
  • Collaborate with Engineering, Product, and Solution Enablement teams to translate requirements into robust test plans.
  • Identify potential edge cases, failure points, and system-level risks early in the development lifecycle.

Automation Development

  • Design and implement automated test suites (unit, integration, regression, performance, end-to-end).
  • Write test automation in Python/JavaScript and integrate into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Build reusable test frameworks that scale across multiple products and teams.

AI-Powered QA & Innovation

  • Research, evaluate, and implement AI-driven QA tools and methodologies.
  • Apply AI to test generation, anomaly detection, log analysis, and continuous validation.
  • Champion best practices for AI-enabled QA within the company.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with engineers to ensure test coverage and quality gates are embedded in the development process.
  • Work closely with Product to define acceptance criteria and verify business-critical workflows.
  • Proactively communicate quality status, risks, and improvements to leadership.

Continuous Improvement

  • Drive a culture of quality and reliability across the organization.
  • Document test cases, frameworks, and QA processes for knowledge sharing.
  • Stay ahead of emerging QA automation trends, tools, and AI technologies.

A Day in the Life

Morning

  • Review overnight CI/CD test runs, investigate failures, and triage issues.
  • Meet with Engineering to discuss new feature test coverage.

Late Morning

  • Develop automated test scripts for a new API integration.
  • Explore an AI-based tool for generating synthetic test data.

Afternoon

  • Run end-to-end validation on a new customer-facing automation workflow.
  • Host a short sync with Product to clarify acceptance criteria.

End of Day

  • Document reusable test patterns.
  • Research the latest in AI-assisted QA frameworks and propose experiments.

Required Experience (Key Skills & Qualifications)

Technical

  • 3+ years of experience in QA, software engineering, or test automation.
  • Strong programming skills in Python and/or JavaScript.
  • Solid understanding of APIs, system integrations, and test automation frameworks.
  • Experience with CI/CD systems (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI).
  • Familiarity with AI/ML-driven testing tools (or strong desire to learn and implement).

Analytical & Collaborative

  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to break down complex systems into testable components.
  • Excellent communication skills—able to partner with engineers, product managers, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Detail-oriented and relentless about ensuring product quality.

Mindset

  • Self-motivated, resourceful, and curious about new technologies.
  • Comfortable working in a dynamic startup environment.
  • Passionate about automation, AI, and building high-quality software.

This is a remote position based out of Pakistan.

title: Remote Market Research Interviewer
description:
Work remotely from anywhere in the UK

£15.99 per hour*

Full or part-time day shifts

Spaces are limited, we encourage early applications as this role will close once we receive sufficient applications.

About us

IFF is an award-winning social research agency, that helps organisations, businesses and individuals make better informed decisions. We deliver best-in-class social research on topics that really matter, helping shape public policy and informing programmes and initiatives that make a difference to people’s lives.

About the role

Working from home you’ll carry out telephone interviews on behalf of our social research team. This will involve calling a predetermined list of people and asking them a set list of questions and recording their answers. We’ll give you a script to follow and you’ll record the responses accurately.

This isn’t cold calling, it’s important work that captures information from different audiences and helps organisations like government departments make better, more informed decisions.

The role requires accuracy, great communication skills and integrity.

This is a fully remote role, it is essential that you have a computer or laptop to work from (not a tablet or phone), a USB headset and an Ethernet connection. You also must be able to work from a UK location.

The role offers a paid training session over 1 day. Successful people will be able to book shifts on a weekly basis. Shifts for this role are Monday – Friday 9am to 4.30pm, some shorter shifts will also be available but aren’t guaranteed.

About you

You must be a great communicator and will be happy speaking to a variety of people, it would be helpful if you have experience in telephone interviewing, market research, customer service, outbound calling, telesales or contact centre environments but it’s not essential as we’ll give you full training.

You must be confident using a computer and will be able to record information accurately and quickly and you’ll be happy to work to targets.

What’s in it for you?

  • Flexible shifts – full or short daytime shifts to suit your schedule

·Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Above Real Living Wage – £14.27 per hour + holiday pay (£15.99 + bonuses) after training
  • Full training & daily support – we set you up for success

·Achievable bonuses

  • A friendly, supportive team culture – plus social activities & wellbeing resources

What’s next:

Complete our application form in full and you’ll be sent to our online assessment stage, which focuses on your customer service and telephone skills. We’ll make our decision based on these outcomes.
If you're successful at this stage you'll be invited for a paid live trial training session.

*Note: Your live trial and training period will be paid at our training rate of £12.71 plus holiday. If you successfully pass the training period you'll be paid at the hourly rate of £14.27 plus holiday which is £15.99.

title: Ramp Tower Controller - Air Traffic Strategy
description:
Achieving our goals starts with supporting yours. Grow your career, access top-tier health and wellness benefits, build lasting connections with your team and our customers, and travel the world using our extensive route network.

Come join us to create what’s next. Let’s define tomorrow, together.

Description

Our Network Operations team works around the clock running United’s global operation, safely, reliably and efficiently. From dispatching and routing our fleet to coordinating with maintenance line planning and crew scheduling, this team makes caring connections with our internal customers and ultimately, United’s customers. From pushback to landing, the Network Operations team is the eyes and ears on the ground no matter where in the world your United flight takes you.

Job overview and responsibilities


The Ramp Tower Controller’s primary purpose is to coordinate and administer ramp control and gate management throughout the geographic boundaries of the airport non-movement area on a per shift basis and serve as the focal point for the safe, efficient, and expeditious ground movement of aircraft ingress and egress within the confines of the ramp to achieve operational priorities. Through effective flow of arrivals and departures will improve on-time performance and reduce taxi delays. Proper sequencing of departures ensures high value flights receive necessary priority without impact to airport surface movement. Arrival performance is vastly improved as controllers use all available tools to make prioritized decisions to maximize ramp and gate space.

  • Serves as the focal point for the safe, efficient, and expeditious ground movement of aircraft ingress and egress within the confines of the ramp
  • Monitors inbound and outbound operations and determines best course of action to manage movement, issuing push, taxi, safety advisories, and instructions to aircraft in the non-movement area via FCC licensed frequencies
  • Communicates and interacts effectively with local internal departments, specifically the Stations Operations Center, Network Operations Center, and ATS Desk on flight priority and resource capabilities
  • Maintains continuous liaison with the local airport authority, local FAA, other airlines, deice companies, and any other entity necessary to ensure the smooth operation of the ramp tower functions
  • Works with specialized hardware and software, including video cameras, aircraft monitoring systems, gate management systems, and VHF radio equipment to safely communicate, monitor, and control aircraft movement
  • Maintains currency in changes to the airfield layout, construction, and aircraft management policies and procedures associated with the operations of the ramp tower
  • Provides ramp control services to other airlines under United control areas
  • Backfills for operational manager as Controller in Charge (CIC) as needed and other duties as assigned

Qualifications

What’s needed to succeed (Minimum Qualifications):

  • High School Diploma, GED, or education equivalent
  • 2 years' experience in Airline/Airport Operations and/or an aviation-related college degree
  • Intimate knowledge of Airline/Airport operations
  • Ability to read, write, and clearly speak the English language
  • Ability to multitask different operations at the same time
  • Technology literate in working within established systems
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment
  • Must be flexible and willing to work any shift in a 24 hour/7 day a week operation including weekends, nights and holidays
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without sponsorship
  • Successful completion of interview required to meet job qualification
  • Reliable, punctual attendance is an essential function of the position

What will help you propel from the pack (Preferred Qualifications):

  • College Degree with aviation focus
  • Aviation Management
  • Previous Ramp Tower or FAA Air Traffic Control

The base pay range for this role is $66,500.00 to $86,616.00.
The base salary range/hourly rate listed is dependent on job-related, factors such as experience, education, and skills. This position is also eligible for bonus and/or long-term incentive compensation awards.

You may be eligible for the following competitive benefits: medical, dental, vision, life, accident & disability, parental leave, employee assistance program, commuter, paid holidays, paid time off, 401(k) and flight privileges.

description:
The next part of your journey is right around the corner — with The Standard.

A genuine desire to make a difference in the lives of others is the foundation for everything we do. With a customer-first mindset and an intentional focus on building strong teams, we’ve been able to uphold our legacy of financial stability while investing in new, innovative technologies that support the needs of our customers. Job Summary

Join our Corporate Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) team, reporting to the Director of Corporate FP&A, as a senior individual contributor with end-to-end ownership of enterprise operating expense planning, forecasting, variance analysis, and management reporting. The role serves as a trusted resource for their peers, helping elevate analytical quality and strengthen process discipline. This individual will build deep expertise in operating expense drivers, allocation methodologies, enterprise financials, foundational data models, and complex consolidations. Over time, they will identify opportunities to streamline and improve core FP&A processes, creating capacity for deeper analysis, stronger business partnership, and supporting the team's continued growth and evolution.

Education: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Analytics, or a related field required, Master's degree preferred.

Experience: 5+ years of progressive experience in corporate finance, FP&A, financial reporting, accounting, or related financial analysis functions.

  • Strong financial and accounting knowledge with the ability to independently evaluate results and challenge assumptions.

  • Experience leading complex financial processes, managing multiple workstreams, maintaining momentum, and communicating status effectively.

  • Clear and concise communication skills with experience preparing executive-level analyses, presentations, and recommendations.

In addition to the competitive salary range below, our employee-focused benefits support work-life balance. Learn more about working at The Standard.

title: 22172 - Delivery Manager

description:
Working Arrangements & Further Information

The MoJ offers Hybrid Working arrangements where business need allows. This is an informal, non-contractual form of flexible working that blends working from your base location, different MoJ sites and / or from home (please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas). All employees will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of their working time in an office, subject to local estate capacity.

Some roles will not be suitable for Hybrid Working. Similarly, Hybrid Working will not suit everyone’s circumstances. Arrangements will be discussed and agreed with the successful candidate(s) and subject to regular review.

For nationally advertised role: all successful candidates will be appointed to the nearest viable office nearest to their home postcode and on its respective pay scale. This will be at either a HQ building (subject to desk allocation, a Justice Collaboration Centre (JCC) or a Justice Satellite Office (JSO) – See Map. All employees will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of their working time in an office, subject to local estate capacity).

For current MoJ employees, your base location will need to be changed to the nearest viable office (to your home postcode), either at a HQ building, JCC or JSO within the National Office Network and moved its location’s respective pay scale (any legacy arrangements/locations will need to be amended).

Some of MoJ’s terms and conditions of service are changing as part of Civil Service reform. The changes will apply to staff joining MoJ who are new to the Civil Service. Staff joining MoJ from other civil service employers will transfer onto the new MoJ terms if they are already on 'modernised' terms in their current post or onto 'unmodernised' MoJ terms if they are on 'unmodernised' terms at their current post. Details will be available if an offer is made.

MoJ candidates who are on a specialist grade, will be able to retain their grade on lateral transfer.

All candidates who are currently in receipt of Mark Time / Pay Protection should ensure they are familiar with the new policy on permanent and temporary promotion which can be found on the employee intranet.

Flexible working hours

The Ministry of Justice offers a flexible working system in many offices. Standard full time working hours are 37 hours per week. MoJ welcomes part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns, where they meet the demands of the role and business needs. All applications for part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns will be considered in accordance with the MoJ’s Flexible Working policy.

Benefits

The MoJ offers a range of benefits:

Annual Leave

Annual leave is 25 days on appointment and will increase to 30 days after five years’ service.

There is also a scheme to allow qualifying staff to buy or sell up to three days leave each year. Additional paid time off for public holidays and 1 privilege day. Leave for part-time and job share posts will be calculated on a pro-rata basis.

Pension

The Civil Service offers a choice of pension schemes, giving you the flexibility to choose the pension that suits you best.

Training

The Ministry of Justice is committed to staff development and offers an extensive range of training and development opportunities.

Networks

The opportunity to join employee-run networks that have been established to provide advice and support and to enable the views of employees from minority groups to be expressed direct to senior management. There are currently networks for employees of minority ethnic origin, employees with disabilities, employees with caring responsibilities, women employees, and lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender employees.

Support

  • A range of ‘Family Friendly’ policies such as opportunities to work reduced hours or job share.
  • Access to flexible benefits such as voluntary benefits, retail vouchers and discounts on a range of goods and services.
  • For moves to or from another employer or moves across the Civil Service this can have implications on your eligibility to carry on claiming childcare vouchers. You may however be eligible for alternative government childcare support schemes, including Tax Free Childcare. More information can be found on or Childcare Choices. You can determine your eligibility at .
  • Paid paternity, adoption and maternity leave.
  • Free annual sight tests for employees who use computer screens.

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. Should you feel that the recruitment process has breached the recruitment principles you are able to raise a formal complaint in the following order

  • To Transformative Business Services (0345 241 5359 (Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm) or e mail moj-recruitment-vetting-enquiries@resourcing.soprasteria.co.uk);
  • To Ministry of Justice Resourcing team (resourcing-management-office@justice.gov.uk);
  • To the Civil Service Commission (details available here)

As a Disability Confident employer, MoJ are committed to providing everyone with the opportunity to demonstrate their skills, talent and abilities, by making adjustments throughout all elements of the recruitment process and in the workplace. MoJ are able to offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns.

For more information on applying for a role as a candidate with a disability or long-term condition, please watch our animated videos.

You will be able to request reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process within the application form. If you need additional help completing the application form, please contact the TBS Recruitment Enquiries Team.

Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.

A Great Place to Work for Veterans

The "Making the Civil Service a Great Place to work for veterans" initiative includes a guaranteed interview scheme to those who meet the minimum criteria to provide eligible former members of the Armed Forces with opportunities to secure rewarding jobs. Allowing veterans to continue to serve their country, and to bring highly skilled individuals with a broad range of experience into the Civil Service in an environment, which recognises and values your previous service in the Armed Forces.
For further details about the initiative and eligibility requirements visit:

Redeployment Interview Scheme

Civil Service departments are expected to explore redeployment opportunities before making an individual redundant. The MoJ is committed, as part of the Redeployment Interview Scheme, to providing opportunities to those who are 'at risk of redundancy'.

MoJ is able to offer an interview to eligible candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns. Candidates will not be eligible for the Redeployment Interview Scheme if they are applying on promotion.

Civil Service Nationality Rules

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals
  • nationals of the Republic of Ireland
  • nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/settled-status-eu-citizens-families
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities who have made a valid application for settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS)
  • individuals with limited leave to remain or indefinite leave to remain who were eligible to apply for EUSS on or before 31 December 2020
  • Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service

Further information on nationality requirements (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/nationality-rules

Reserve list

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made for the same or similar roles.

title: Precision Cleaning Technician - (Overnight Shift)
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

PRECISION CLEANING TECHNICIAN

The Cleanroom Technician is a member of the Mechanical Production Team but is specifically focused on the precision cleaning of Reaction Wheels and Electron Components.

You can expect to receive world class training according to Rocket Lab standards and processes. We are an all-inclusive and equal opportunity employer, supporting career development, training and merit-based internal progression.

Must be comfortable working the overnight shift (21:00 - 07:30). Night shift allowance in effect.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

  • Precision cleaning of mechanical components
  • Inspection of cleaned items
  • Work in a pristine environment
  • Support the development of new processes
  • Enjoy a 4 day week, 3 day weekend

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Comfortable working to exacting standards
  • Have a good level of eyesight and an eye for detail

THESE SKILLS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
  • The ability to work effectively in a team environment as well as autonomously
  • Knowledge of ultrasonic cleaners, precision cleaning, oxygen cleaning and clean room methodologies
  • A high work ethic, always seeking more responsibility. Able to work overtime if required
  • Takes initiative and remains calm under pressure
  • Computer literate, and comfortable using smartphones and tablets

If you're a quick learner with an eye for detail, apply now! We can teach the rest!

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

title: Workplace Design Specialist
description:
Job Overview

We are seeking a motivated, detail-oriented, and design-driven Federal & Workplace Design Specialist to join our team. In this role, you will develop your technical skills, learn complex contract processes, and support the execution of GSA, public sector, and government contract projects. Representing a top-tier U.S. commercial furniture dealer handling premier brands like Haworth, Steelcase, Kimball, and Teknion, you will work closely with senior design staff to translate client requirements into compliant, high-performance commercial and federal workplace environments.

As an entry-to-junior-level professional, you will learn to manage contract-aligned documentation, navigate product compliance, and build your expertise in systems furniture. Partnering with senior designers and Account Executives, you will assist in producing workspace solutions, space plans, and visual presentations that support high-visibility contracts.

Key Responsibilities

  • Visuals & Plans: Assist in the development of detailed CET drawings, furniture plans, product specifications, 3D visuals, and client presentation materials.
  • GSA & Code Compliance: Support space planning efforts by learning to integrate systems furniture, architectural plans, commercial codes (ADA, LEED, WELL), and specific government procurement requirements under the guidance of senior team members.
  • Documentation & Installation Packages: Help produce detailed installation drawings and specification packages, ensuring accuracy, constructability, and alignment with project intent.
  • Field Coordination: Participate in field verifications, inventories, and onsite measurements. Help identify and document discrepancies between plans and actual field conditions.
  • Cross-Functional Teamwork: Partner with senior designers, Account Executives, and internal teams to execute project visions and solve design challenges.
  • Professional Growth: Actively participate in client-facing meetings and coordination discussions alongside senior team members to build confidence and presentation skills.
  • Project Tracking: Provide proactive, regular updates to Design Managers, Team Leads, and senior designers regarding project status, deadlines, and task completion.
  • Mentorship Absorption: Actively seek feedback, participate in drawing reviews, and learn from technical guidance, product knowledge, and process coaching provided by Designer III team members.
  • Quality Control: Adhere to established design standards, workflow processes, and quality control checklists to ensure all deliverables are accurate before release.
  • Market Learning: Develop a baseline understanding of product innovations, workplace ergonomics, manufacturer resources, and sustainability considerations.


Qualifications:


  • Education: Bachelor's degree from a FIDER or CIDA-accredited interior design program or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Experience: 0–2 years of industry experience, preferably with exposure to commercial interiors, furniture dealership projects, or workplace design solutions. (Internship experience in a similar environment is a major plus).
  • Software Expertise: Proficiency in AutoCAD (basic drawing production, layers, and blocks). Familiarity with, or a strong willingness to learn, CET Designer (Configura) and ProjectSpec.
  • Product & Sector Knowledge: Basic understanding of or strong interest in systems furniture, ancillary solutions, finish selections, and public sector/GSA environments.
  • Mindset & Soft Skills: Highly organized, eager to learn, and possessive of strong communication and problem-solving skills. Ability to take direction well, ask clarifying questions, and thrive in a collaborative team setting.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive Pay and Benefits.
  • Opportunity to work with cutting-edge design technology.
  • Thrive in a fast-paced, supportive team that values work-life balance.
  • Play a key role in design operations—your impact on company growth will be evident.
  • Join a culture that values your contributions and equips you with the tools to succeed.
  • Be part of an innovative team that continuously learns and adapts.

title: Data Modeler
description:
Ippon Australia is a team of true technologists who leverage contemporary thinking and tools to enhance the way our clients drive value. Whether it’s a bespoke platform to improve employee engagement within a national retail chain, or developing an app that provides next level direct customer interaction; value is delivered to our clients when we begin by understanding the business outcomes they desire and then apply our technical expertise to make these a reality. We are expanding our market offering through the development of a Data Driven Architecture practice and are searching for passionate Data Modeller to join the team.

Ippon is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive culture that encourages, celebrates and supports our diversity everyday.
